messages:
sandeep: FYI customer reported a surge of 504s hitting hosted API for tenant 'foodly'. They say requests succeed intermittently but most get timeouts. Started ~14:02 UTC. Symptoms look like tail timeouts, p95 fine but p99+ exploding.

eli: Can you paste the gateway logs? any 502/503 or internal 504s?

sandeep: Pasting trimmed logs from gateway:```\n> 2026-03-15T14:02:17Z ingress-gw request_id=abc123 tenant=foodly status=202 latency_ms=12\n> 2026-03-15T14:02:18Z ingress-gw request_id=abc124 tenant=foodly status=504 downstream_error=queue_timeout\n> 2026-03-15T14:02:18Z ingress-gw request_id=abc125 tenant=foodly status=504 downstream_error=kv_cache_miss\n> 2026-03-15T14:02:19Z ingress-gw request_id=abc126 tenant=foodly status=202 latency_ms=15\n> 2026-03-15T14:02:20Z ingress-gw request_id=abc127 tenant=foodly status=504 downstream_error=batcher_backlog\n```

miriam: Interesting, logs show explicit queue_timeout + kv_cache_miss + batcher_backlog. Could be continuous batching backlog + KV cache thrash causing some requests to be pushed past queue_depth limit.

dan: I just checked serving runtime metrics for the affected pool: batcher_queue_length spiked to ~480 (limit is 500), continuous_batch_window increased from 8ms->120ms, kv_cache_evictions spiked. p99 token latency jumped.

eli: So the sequence is: tenant traffic surge -> batcher keeps growing window to maximize throughput -> KV cache eviction increases (misses) -> some requests cause longer generation times -> queue depth hits hard reject -> gateway returns 504.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-033-94 (severity: high) assigned to eng-runtime.

miriam: Repro steps suggested by support: small steady traffic + a few very long-context requests triggered it. Support provided a repro curl that hits a ~2048 token prompt.

support-bot: Customer repro: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input": "<2k tokens>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` repeated 120 req/s for 30s.

dan: Ok. Short-term mitigation options: 1) enable tenant-level early_reject when queue_depth>420, 2) reduce continuous_batch_max_window from 120ms->30ms for the pool, 3) increase kv_cache_size or change LRU threshold. Which can we flip fastest?

eli: We can toggle early_reject on the gateway via feature flag in ~2 minutes. Batch window requires deploying a config to the batcher (no restart, just config push) — ~10 minutes. Increasing kv_cache_size requires planning and might be heavy if memory constrained.

miriam: Let's do early_reject now to prevent more tail timeouts. Then reduce batch window to cap latency. Also bump eviction threshold temporarily.

sandeep: I'm rolling the feature flag: `feature.gateway.early_reject.v1=true` scoped to pool=hosted-prod-3 and tenant=foodly. Pushing... done.

ops-bot: Feature flag toggle recorded by deploy-bot at 2026-03-15T14:06:02Z.

eli: After early_reject, 504s should become immediate 429s for excess traffic (better for client retry logic). Anyone see traffic pattern change?

dan: Monitoring: within 60s, 504 rate dropped by ~75%, 429 increased. p99 token latency decreased from ~3.2s -> 1.1s. kv_cache_evictions still elevated but not exploding.

miriam: Good. Next step: reduce continuous_batch_max_window for the pool to 30ms. I'll push config to batcher. Config snippet:```json\n{"batcher":{"continuous_max_window_ms":30}}\n```

miriam: Pushed config at 14:12. No restart required.

eli: Observing batcher behavior now: batch sizes down by ~40%, window bounded, per-token latency stable. tail timeouts nearly gone.

sandeep: Customer confirms reduced error rate in their environment — sending logs showing 429s replaced 504s and overall success rate up.

dan: Medium-term: we should add per-tenant policy that prevents long-context heavy jobs from joining latency-sensitive pools — route them to a dedicated long-running model pool or apply per-request max_tokens hint. Also consider adaptive kv cache per-tenant.

miriam: Agreed. Filing follow-up action items: A) add tenant-aware routing rule (owner: eli) B) improve KV cache observability + per-tenant caps (owner: dan) C) default early_reject as safety net for pools (owner: sandeep).

eli: I'll take A. ETA: PR and canary config by tomorrow.

dan: I'll take B — will instrument kv cache hit/miss per-tenant and add an autosize alert. ETA: 2 weeks.

sandeep: I'll draft the default early_reject rollout doc and a runbook for support to flip flags. ETA: EOD.

support-bot: Customer notified at 2026-03-15T15:01:00Z: workaround applied, request to monitor for 24h.

miriam: Marking this incident as mitigated. Adding postmortem tags: continuous-batching, kv-cache, early_reject. Will follow up with a short postmortem doc.

eli: Thanks team. If anyone needs the raw traces/logs I saved them to /mnt/logs/incidents/2265432100.tgz.

sandeep: Closing thread; reopen if errors recur. :thumbsup:
